directory_deadlock.cause: The caller held a filesystem read guard while invoking parent/mount resolution, which could recursively read the same namespace. A queued writer could block that read while waiting for the first guard.
directory_deadlock.fix: A closed helper returns owned child metadata; parent/mount resolution and encoding hold no namespace guard.

negative_control.method: Same corrected concurrent regression test on an isolated committed, unfixed runtime; 5-second progress deadline, no quota failure.

directory_deadlock.fixture_note: Final regression uses 512 created names, within the existing 1024-node memory fixture limit. An initial version exceeded the fixture quota; no production quota was changed.

directory_deadlock.timing_protocol: Directory hot-loop comparisons explicitly use --prepare-directory to create identical contents sequentially. Cold concurrent creation is separately validated six times on the final real HVF runner. The failed baseline and negative-control results are retained, not treated as timings.

method: Four processes each perform 1,000 checked operations; three unprofiled counterbalanced before/after repetitions, longest-child loop median and process-wall median. Separate diagnostic samples include startup/teardown. Linux-only signalfd APIs use the exact static musl ELF on the existing six-vCPU ARM64 local Linux CI environment as native reference; no native macOS signalfd API is substituted. The CI VM is stopped during Mac timings. No whole-app, Firefox or physical iPad speedup inference.
